It's difficult to illustrate this, but I've been trying out different vision-based image stabilisation routines (detecting the horizon and deriving orientation from that, vs gyro data). Tried various elaborate algorithms / ML routines, but its Otsu's method that clearly won...

It turns out, for my purposes, the most generally robust method is simply dividing the image between the dark ground and the light sky (as pictured), and deriving the horizon based on the average middle. No other algorithm performed as robustly in my noisy test environment (aka street horizon).

When I write up this project, I'm going to talk at length about this, because you can do a really interesting critical code reading of different stabilising algorithms, inc. ML-based, and their working in different worldly contexts - as vignettes of the perennial limits of computing prehension.
